label: D1 reward after an a2 trial that the agent will repeat (rare-rewarded a2, or very late in episode)
explanation: Fires only at D1, only when the reward input is 1, and almost only when the previous choice was a2 (90% of mass) and the upcoming choice is again a2 (99% of mass). It is silent at GO and D2, after unrewarded trials, and after a1 trials. The largest activations come after a rare-rewarded a2 trial (a2 led to S1 and S1 paid), when the agent nevertheless stays with a2. Small activations also build up gradually over streaks of rewarded common a2->S2 trials. There is a strong episode-time dependence: it is essentially silent before trial ~40 and has 6x lift in trials 90-99, so I think it reflects slow drift in the hidden state. It also fires most when value is low and the choice logit is mildly in favour of a2. The predicate uses action (the upcoming choice of the agent itself, a legitimate computed quantity). Without the action term, using only observed variables, dev F1 is 0.67 vs 0.71 with it. Dev: P 0.63, R 0.82, F1 0.71, mass recall 0.88.
